source_text: Quod ut claruit Apostolum dixisse de moribus, ita apparet quanta testimoniorum Legis inopia labores, qui ab his sententiis contra fulmina rationis opem petis, quae tibi dedignantur, immo natura sui subvenire non possunt.
pass_a_gloss: Which as it has become clear that the Apostle said about manners, so it appears with how great a want of testimonies of the Law you labor, who from these sentences against the thunderbolts of reason seek help, which disdain you, nay by their own nature cannot come under.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Just as it has become clear that the apostle said this about conduct, so it is apparent how desperately you lack the Law's testimonies. Against reason's thunderbolts you seek help from statements that disdain to assist you, indeed cannot assist you by their very nature.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
